title: Tags & note — built for real, across the app

steps.path: Click the tag element in the bottom status bar
steps.headline: The approved design, now the real popup: tag pills, "+ New tag", a Note card and Pin to top.
steps.changed: Every tag is a pill: × takes it off, + puts it on, grey means archived. Priority is gone from the list; it's the Pin to top switch now. No Done button — changes save as you make them. The pills now fill the row before wrapping (your round-15 note).
steps.notice: Everything about this session's tags is in one place, and nothing needs saving.
steps.risk: Clicking a tag's name opens its edit box; only the × or + switches it on or off.

steps.headline: Clicking a tag opens its edit box inside the Tags card, with a full colour picker.
steps.changed: Name, the ten colours plus a rainbow circle for any colour you like, Archived, then red Delete tag on the left and Cancel / Save on the right. Delete asks first.
steps.notice: Rename or recolour a tag without leaving the popup. Custom colours are new.
steps.risk: A custom colour isn't tuned per theme the way the ten are, so a very dark or very pale pick can be faint on some themes.

steps.headline: "+ New tag" opens a New tag box in the same spot; the new tag goes straight onto this session.
steps.changed: Name and colour, red Cancel on the left, Create on the right. Create with no name shows a short red line instead of greying out.
steps.notice: Typing a new name in the search box and pressing Create still works too.

steps.path: Resume → the tag icon on a conversation
steps.headline: Resume's organize sheet is the same Tags, Note and Pin to top cards as the popup.
steps.changed: The old checkbox list, "pins to top" Priority row and "Manage tags…" link are gone. A pinned conversation shows a small pin in its top-right corner.
steps.notice: Organizing works the same wherever you do it: status bar, Resume, the close prompt, the side panel and Projects.
steps.risk: The sheet is taller than before, so on a small window you scroll a little more to reach the next conversation.

steps.path: Close a session (the × on its tab)
steps.headline: The close prompt shows a pin instead of a yellow Priority tag, and tags in the new pill look.
steps.changed: The summary row reads: pin (if pinned), the tags, the note. The pencil opens the same shared editor with a Save button at the bottom.
steps.notice: Pinned and tagged are visibly two different things now.

steps.path: Click the session name at the top of the window
steps.headline: In the session list, tags use the new pill look and a pinned session shows a pin by its status.
steps.changed: Priority no longer appears as a tag. A session with 3 or more tags shows one small stacked-tags button that rolls out into the full tags when you point at it (no session in this sample has 3).
steps.notice: Long tag rows don't crowd the session name any more.
steps.risk: With 3+ tags you have to point at the stack to read them.

steps.path: The bottom strip of the window
steps.headline: The status bar's tag element is now icons only: a pin, stacked tag colours, and a note page when there's a note.
steps.changed: "Priority +1" became a pin and one blue tag icon. Each icon appears only when it applies; with nothing set it reads "Add tags".
steps.notice: Narrower, and you can tell pinned, tagged and noted apart at a glance.
steps.risk: Tag names aren't shown in the strip; you see colours, and open the popup for names.

steps.path: Conversation cards Claude shows in a reply
steps.headline: Tags shown anywhere else in the app use the same new look.
steps.changed: The square boxes became the rounded pills with a coloured tag icon, matching the session status pills.
steps.notice: One tag look across the whole app.
